executive_summary.overview: Citibank operates a focused US branch network of approximately 648-670 locations concentrated in major metropolitan markets, representing a strategic shift from broad geographic coverage to premium positioning in key business hubs. This contrasts sharply with the 4,000+ branch networks of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo.

key_geographic_findings: Citibank operates 648-670 branches in 13 US states, ranking 16th by branch count - dramatically smaller footprint than top 3 US banks with 4,000+ branches each
Strategic concentration in 6 major metros: NYC, LA, SF, Chicago, Miami, DC - premium positioning rather than mass-market coverage
Branch network stable with minimal closures and selective new openings (e.g., first new Chicago branch in decade)
International presence of 160+ countries represents competitive advantage and differentiator vs. domestically-focused competitors
Exiting consumer banking in 14 international markets while maintaining institutional banking globally aligns with services-led strategy
Limited US branch footprint is strategic choice enabling focus on high-value markets and avoiding low-margin mass-market retail banking
Digital banking platform extends effective reach beyond 648-670 physical locations
Geographic strategy matches overall positioning: premium institutional/commercial bank in key markets rather than ubiquitous retail bank
data_sources: Citigroup press releases and investor materials
methodology_notes: This geographic distribution analysis synthesizes branch location data from multiple sources (Bank Branch Locator, FDIC data, Citigroup official communications) with strategic context from earnings calls and investor presentations. Branch count figures show minor variation across sources (648-670 range) but consistently demonstrate Citi's focused major metro strategy vs. competitors' broad geographic coverage.
